absent: Full device power structure layout and locking for concurrent wakeup flag updates
Active printk backend, log buffer growth and console driver handshaking when enabled
Static call runtime patching order and architecture trampoline code generation
Ratelimit interval and burst tuning values and time source
Dynamic debug enablement evaluation and hex dump output formatting

findings.text: Device power state carries a capability flag plus an arming indicator. Readiness requires both capability and arming. One build variant tests arming by presence of an attached wakeup object, another tests a boolean request flag managed by enable, disable and set helpers. Capability is directly readable and writable.

Wakeup path and out of band markers are latched indicators with query and set operations. Awake path aliases are thin forwards to the wakeup path operations. Event helpers forward to device or object variants with a non urgent marker, except the hard variant which signals urgency with zero delay.

Initialization offers a two state lifecycle. Requesting activation marks the device capable then arms wakeup and propagates the arming outcome. Requesting deactivation disarms first then clears capability and always reports success. A cleanup callback simply requests deactivation for managed release.
Managed helper first requests activation then enrolls a deactivation callback for automatic teardown, reporting only the enrollment outcome.
Single header length limit equals two. Device kmsg string size limit equals ten.

Level detection looks at the first two characters for a start marker followed by a digit in range zero through seven or a continuation marker, yielding that marker or zero when absent. Skipping advances past one such prefix when present, and header skipping repeats until no prefix remains.

Silent console threshold is zero, minimum usable is one, debug is ten, most verbose is fifteen. Default console, quiet console and default message thresholds are build configuration values rather than fixed numbers.
Four console thresholds share one array in fixed order. Current console, default message, minimum console and default console occupy slots zero through three respectively.
Variadic carrier holds two references in order. Member fmt carries the template pointer. Member va carries the pointer to the argument list.
Distinct textual markers exist for firmware bug, firmware warning, firmware information, hardware error and deprecated usage notices, each intended as a message prefix.

Degraded logging build provides callable no operation entry points that discard output. Formatted and variadic print variants report zero length, early output does nothing, and the format checking helper evaluates its arguments in dead code while reporting zero.

Degraded auxiliary services are inert with neutral outcomes. Deferred and forced console transitions, klog wake, buffer setup, stack and register dumps, flush triggers, replay, panic sync, release and unsafe atomic flush do nothing. Address lookup yields null, length lookup yields zero, rate checks deny, timed rate denies, console acquire denies, and flush completion claims success.

Cpu print synchronization in this variant is always immediately available with empty wait and release. The interrupt safe acquisition loop saves interrupts, tests availability, restores and waits on contention until success. Release pairs synchronization release with interrupt restore.

Index entry is packed. Member fmt holds message template. Member func holds function name. Member file holds file name. Member line holds line number. Member level holds optional level with null meaning embedded in template. Member subsys_fmt_prefix holds subsystem prefix.

Default prefix formatter is identity. Index emission has an active variant that records constant templates with location and level into a dedicated section, and an inert variant that discards all arguments. Subsystem and generic wrappers record then forward to the chosen print routine, with deferred printing bound to the deferred routine.

Severity wrappers attach the matching kernel level to a formatted message after applying the file prefix, covering emergency through informational plus a continuation form that omits the file prefix. Development messages follow the same path when enabled and are discarded otherwise.
Debug wrapper has three build variants. One uses dynamic control, one prints directly at debug level, and one discards output entirely.

Once wrappers emit only on first execution via a once gate, including deferred once. Severity, development and debug once forms layer the once gate over their normal level handling, with disabled builds discarding output.

Ratelimited wrappers gate output through a per call site token bucket using default interval and burst, emitting only when the gate allows. Severity, development and debug ratelimited forms layer that gate over level handling, with disabled builds discarding and one dynamic debug variant requiring both dynamic enablement and gate approval.
Hex dump prefix selector offers three ordered modes for no prefix, address prefix and offset prefix.

Hex dump helpers share level, prefix, geometry, buffer and ascii controls. Degraded build provides inert stubs. Debug selection chooses among dynamic control, fixed debug level forwarding and inert stub. Development selection chooses between debug level forwarding and inert stub. Byte helper forwards to debug form with sixteen byte rows, single byte groups and ascii enabled.

Module node chains via member next. Member mod identifies owner with null meaning core. Member sites references patch sites. Trampoline key holds member tramp for trampoline offset and member key for key offset, both signed thirty two bit.

Static call abstraction defines a key holding current target plus a type marker set to one alongside an architecture trampoline. Variants cover preset target, null target and zero returning target. Update swaps the target through a trampoline address which is either the real trampoline or null when unavailable, query reads the current target once, conditional invocation touches the call without branching, and export helpers publish key and trampoline symbols including GPL and trampoline only forms. Header guard ensures single inclusion.
External dependency for managed action registration.

Degraded wakeup registration yields null and unregistration plus hold, release and event notifications are inert, so callers must tolerate absent objects and lost wakeups. Degraded console acquisition always denies while flush completion always claims success, so callers must not assume acquisition succeeded from flush outcome.
